messages.subject: Caldervale — strategy and the two killer points
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah, James,

Having been through the contract and their termination letter, two points decide this:

1. Schedule 4 methodology. Their availability figures (98.1% March, 97.4% June, 98.6% Sept) count maintenance windows and an outage on 14 June that our incident log says was THEIR single sign-on failing. Strip those out and we're above 99.5% every month.

2. No clause 16.3 notice. Clause 16.3 needs written notice specifying the breach and 30 days to remedy. Their three emails are service queries, not notices. So even if there were qualifying breaches, the termination is procedurally bad.

I'd plead both. Thoughts before I draft the LBA?

Tom

messages.subject: RE: Caldervale — strategy and the two killer points
messages.plaintextBody:
Agree with both. Point 2 is the cleaner win because it doesn't depend on the monitoring evidence — it's pure contract. Lead with the debt (Milestone 2) as it's unanswerable once acceptance is admitted, then the repudiation. Make sure the LBA asks for their availability monitoring records; if they can't produce methodology-compliant figures, point 1 collapses for them.

James
